title: Time each reveal from aligned speech
statement: Time each on-screen reveal and caption from when the voice says its words, taken from an aligned take, not by spreading them evenly or by sentence length.
example: One pilot bound 14 animation cues to 62 aligned words of a measured take, each cue at its word's start.
detail: A pilot for short narrated films aligned a measured take to its script, 62 aligned words in all, and set each of its 14 animation cues to the start of its word, by its own rule that measured speech times drive the cues (`g9/tools/unit-video-essay/README.md`, `g9/tools/unit-video-essay/INTEGRATION.md`). The lesson engine that later took in the pilot's frame modules spreads each part's reveals evenly across the part's narration and times captions by each sentence's share of the part's characters (`g9/transformer/src/video/beats.js`, `g9/transformer/src/video/produce.js`), although the module contract expects the host to map word-alignment cues. No harm from the even spread has been recorded, so this stays an adopted rule.
against: Timing from an alignment is not approval of the take: the pilot's notes say its generated voice has had no human listening or curriculum sign-off, and "matched alignment flags are not such proof." (g9/tools/unit-video-essay/INTEGRATION.md line 44). The lesson engine's own films spread each part's reveals evenly across its narration and time captions by each sentence's share of the narration's length, and no harm from that has been recorded (`g9/transformer/src/video/beats.js`, `g9/transformer/src/video/produce.js`).
